properties.name: DEFECT (measured 2026-10-01): every served skill's frontmatter carries `metadata: {composes: [..]}`, a LIST, where the Agent Skills spec allows `metadata` only as a string-to-string map — a strict client may skip all 32 skills, and skill_lint has no Agent Skills check
properties.source: served skill text (e.g. get_skill where-am-i, brainstorm, plan-increments return `metadata: {composes: [STANDING, REPORTS], audience: anyone, summary: …}`); agentskills.io specification (metadata: string→string map), re-read in the 2026-10-01 standards look; Agent Plugins spec §7.1 (a non-conforming skill is skipped)
properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-10-01. The served skills open with frontmatter such as `metadata: {composes: [STANDING, REPORTS], audience: anyone, summary: "…"}`. The Agent Skills specification (agentskills.io/specification, unchanged since 2026-08-04) defines `metadata` as a map from string keys to STRING values. `composes` is a YAML list, so every skill carrying it is outside the spec.

WHY IT MATTERS:
- req:reflow2s-skills-conform-to-the-agent-skills-specification (accepted 2026-09-28) says reflow2's own additions are carried "in the way the specification allows for extensions, never in a way that breaks a conforming reader".
- The Agent Plugins spec §7.1 says a skill that does not conform to Agent Skills is SKIPPED. So once reflow2 is packaged as a plugin, a strict client could load none of the 32 skills.
- tools/skill_lint.py enforces reflow2's own contracts but has no Agent Skills conformance check yet, which that requirement asks for.

NOT ROOT-CAUSED AND NOT FIXED. One obvious repair is to encode composes as a string (e.g. "STANDING,REPORTS"). Whether the build's skill composer (build.rs) reads that field, and how, has to be checked before choosing one.
